title: Action Blueprints — compact function-first PRD sketch
content:
TL;DR: Compact "Action Blueprints" = small, reusable structured prompt + function-calling spec that captures common user intents (e.g., create calendar item, summarize thread, extract entities) with the explicit goal of minimizing token usage and predictable latency. Target: hosted API and Dedicated quickstarts where customers want deterministic cost per action and low tail latency.

Context + problem:
- We ship broad capabilities (chat, functions, tools) but many product teams need tiny, repeatable actions. Current flows send a lot of conversational baggage (system + context + long instruction) every time which increases cost and latency.
- Customers building high-volume assistant flows (ticket triage, scheduling, short summaries) ask for guidance to keep functions cheap and fast. They also want easy rollback when model output drifts.
- Opportunity: define canonical compact templates that combine: minimal instruction, canonical output schema, and a small function signature. Provide SDK helpers to assemble inputs and manage small KV prefixes.

Goal: create a library of 6–8 Action Blueprints + SDK glue and docs that reduce median tokens per action by >=40% for targeted flows and lower p99 latency by ~10–20% via smaller payloads and optional prefix caching.

User personas:
- Product engineer at SaaS company: needs deterministic unit cost for 2–5 action types.
- Platform SRE: wants predictable traffic patterns for Dedicated pools; easier autoscaling signals.
- Solutions engineer / customer success: wants examples to onboard quickly and show cost savings.

Core proposition (MVP):
1) Blueprint spec (text): minimal system + instruction, explicit examples (1–2 shots), output JSON schema.
2) Function contract: a tiny typed function sig (1–6 params) with strict types and length caps.
3) SDK helper: buildPayload(blueprint, params, prefix?) that:
   - injects a persistent 128–512 token prefix (optional),
   - enforces max token budget,
   - optionally routes to low-latency model variant (e.g., 7B quantized).
4) Test harness: micro-eval runner and cost/latency reporter (tokens, latency, failure modes).

Example blueprint (sketch):
- Name: "one-line-summary"
- System: "You are a concise summarizer. Return one sentence with user-facing clarity."
- Input params: {"text": string(<=2000 chars), "tone": enum("neutral","simplified") }
- Function: summarize_one_line(text, tone) -> {"summary": string(<=200 chars)}
- Example: input -> output pair (1 short shot)
- Output enforcement: use structured function response with schema validation on SDK side

Why function-first?
- Function responses remove parsing ambiguity and allow us to trim system/instruction tokens during runtime because the SDK enforces shape.
- Deterministic shape enables more aggressive truncation strategies and easier A/B with model variants.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- 6 blueprints implemented (summary, extract-entities, create-event, triage-label, convert-to-markdown, inline-qa) with docs + examples
- SDK helpers for JS + Python with buildPayload and validateResponse routines
- Bench: median tokens/action down 40% vs current naive prompt; p99 latency reduced in hosted by at least 10% for same throughput in internal tests
- E2E examples (sample app + codelab) and a 1-page customer-facing one-pager for solutions team

Metrics to track:
- tokens_per_action (median, p90, p99)
- median_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms for blueprint calls
- function_failure_rate (schema mismatch, missing params)
- adoption: number of customers using blueprints in hosted calls (via tags)

Rough UX flow (for engineer):
1) pick blueprint from console gallery -> view spec -> click "use in code" (JS/Python snippets)
2) SDK preps payload: checks param constraints, attaches optional prefixId token for prefix caching
3) client calls API with model hint for low-latency variant and function schema
4) SDK validates function output; if mismatch, apply fallback mapping to best-effort or forward to full-chat route

Rollout plan (quick):
- Week 0–2: build JS/Python SDK helpers + first 3 blueprints + bench harness
- Week 3: internal dogfooding with SE/CS on 2 pilot customers (support teams, triage flows)
- Week 4–5: add 3 more blueprints, polish docs, add console gallery entry (hosted)
- Week 6: public beta + collection of benchmark numbers and engineer-facing tutorial

Open questions / risks / TODOs (notes to self):
- How aggressive can we be on instructions truncation before model output verges off the schema? Need experiments across 3 model families (7B, 13B, 70B).
- Do we expose a config knob for "safety headroom" that adds N system tokens back for high-sensitivity actions?
- Interaction with Dedicated: prefix caching across requests in a pool — need session affinity or shared cache microservice? Privacy implications for Private deployments.
- Product naming: "Action Blueprints" vs "Action Kits" vs "Compact Functions" — ask PM for preference.
- SDK validation failure UX: raise error vs auto-retry with expanded prompt? Tradeoffs for SLOs.

Quick links/notes:
- Slack: #solutions-engineering pinned sample for event creation (see thread 2025-10-01)
- Jira: RI-2438 = blueprint gallery backend work
- Confluence: draft spec (linked above)

Next steps (my checklist):
- [ ] run small bench: compare naive chat vs function-first blueprint for one-line-summary across 3 seeds
- [ ] prototype JS helper buildPayload (wrap function schema + param validator)
- [ ] sync with Maya on console gallery UX constraints (how many fields, copy, thumbnails)
- [ ] add two-shot examples to prevent hallucination on entity extraction

Voice notes: keep this intentionally scrappy — want something that ships fast and reduces token friction. The long-term play is a composable gallery + rollout templates for customers to pin to Dedicated capacity.

-- Emmet L.
